checks_run: Inventoried and read the 62-file candidate, including learner-facing, evaluator, exercise, reference, harness, benchmark, provenance, and validation material.
Ran python3 environment/verify-structure.py independently; all four structural checks exited 0.
Parsed MANIFEST.yaml, PROVENANCE.json, and both package.json files as strict JSON and recomputed their SHA-256 hashes.
Attempted runtime discovery and the public, sealed, adversarial, and benchmark commands; no Node-compatible runtime or container runner was available.
Counted 21 public and 33 sealed node:test declarations and statically traced the reference dispatcher, request/response helpers, test helpers, adversarial harness, exercises, and benchmark.
Repeated high-confidence credential-signature, credential-assignment, suspicious-key-filename, symlink, and special-file checks.
Compared the manifest, provenance record, license boundary, learner instructions, sealed layout, and builder validation claims.
evidence: The manifest conservatively remains GENERATED/PARTIAL, requires independent validation, and makes no productionization claim; CANDIDATE/VALIDATION.md explicitly disclaims BUILDS, TESTED, FUZZED, BENCHMARKED, REVIEWED, TRANSFER_VERIFIED, and PRODUCTIONIZED.
Independent structure execution reproduced 23 required regular files, 21 forbidden paths absent, 62 files, 25 directories, and strict immutable metadata; all four published file hashes also matched.

Static control-flow tracing found a correctness defect: when decodeURIComponent throws for a captured parameter, dispatch records the error but does not cache the registration match; an arity-four handler later in that same route registration rematches, throws again, and is skipped instead of receiving the URIError.

Twenty-one reference, hidden-test, expectation, fixed-solution, or answer files under sealed paths are directly readable in this submitted artifact. The instructions ask learners not to inspect them, but the candidate contains no learner-export allowlist or access-control/transfer evidence.

The public and sealed helpers use JavaScript timers in the same process as learner code, so a synchronously non-returning handler can prevent the advertised absolute deadline from firing; the in-process benchmark likewise has an iteration cap but no wall-clock watchdog.

The dependency-free CommonJS scaffold, pinned Node 20.19.5 reproduction path, staged public tests, detailed normative requirements, concept notes, and production gap analysis are useful and unusually explicit.

The provenance boundary correctly distinguishes the CC0 catalog from the NOASSERTION linked tutorial and states that linked content was not copied; no credential signature, suspicious key filename, symlink, or special artifact node was observed.
limitations: node, npm, nodejs, bun, deno, qjs, js, Docker, Podman, Apptainer, and Singularity were unavailable; JavaScript syntax and behavior, test passes, adversarial passes, exercise outcomes, and benchmark measurements remain unconfirmed.
Network access and the recorded source checkout were unavailable, so the catalog snapshot, upstream commit contents, linked-resource state, and no-copy assertion could not be independently compared.
No independently produced learner view or transfer artifact was supplied, so external filtering of sealed material could not be assessed.
The generated-material statement describes personal educational use but supplies no explicit reuse/distribution license; legal permission beyond that statement is unresolved.
